riskSignals: No source repository is declared in the JAR metadata.

warnings: A generated plan or successful compile is evidence, not proof of a completed port.
The workspace never mutates the installed mod; changes happen in an isolated copy with hashes and rollback instructions.
Binary-only reconstruction is lower confidence than an upstream source build. Resolve official source and exact dependencies before editing decompiler output whenever possible.
Cross-loader ports require semantic API replacement and side/runtime testing; metadata translation or a compatibility bridge alone is not completion.

tools.name: InterMed
tools.reason: Preflight bytecode, metadata, data/resource, mixin, security, SBOM, log, and performance signals before changing the artifact.
tools.guardrail: Treat findings as evidence to verify, not automatic rewrites.

tools.name: modcrawl
tools.reason: Independent fast JAR metadata, dependency, class, mixin, and duplicate inspection for cross-checking the Vault.

tools.name: Vineflower
tools.reason: Primary modern Java decompiler for source reconstruction; compare its output against a second decompiler and bytecode.

tools.name: CFR
tools.reason: Independent decompiler cross-check to detect control-flow or synthetic-code reconstruction errors.

tools.name: Tiny Remapper
tools.reason: Controlled namespace remapping for compatible mapping graphs.
tools.guardrail: Remapping does not replace semantic API migration.

tools.name: Retromod
tools.reason: Candidate bytecode transforms and compatibility shims for narrow, measured binary gaps.
tools.guardrail: Never call a Retromod-transformed JAR ported until source-equivalent behavior passes the full runtime matrix.

tools.name: ModDevGradle
tools.reason: Official NeoForge development plugin with target-version run and test configuration.

tools.name: Modstitch
tools.reason: Can reduce duplicated source while translating selected loader declarations and access mechanisms.
tools.guardrail: Generated translation must be compared against a native target-loader implementation.

tools.name: japicmp
tools.reason: Binary API diffing across dependency and loader versions to turn compile failures into an ordered migration map.

tools.name: packwiz
tools.reason: Reproducible disposable client/server integration packs for matrix testing.

tools.name: Ferium
tools.reason: Independent Modrinth/CurseForge/GitHub acquisition path for test fixtures and comparison against provider resolution.

phases.title: Preserve and identify
phases.goal: Freeze exact inputs before any mutation.
actions: Hash every input and dependency
Extract loader metadata, mappings, mixins, access rules, services, native libraries, and source provenance
Record source and target toolchain coordinates
gates: Original bytes are unchanged and independently recoverable
Every input has SHA-256 and SHA-512 identity

phases.title: Reconstruct the exact source environment
phases.goal: Make the original artifact reproducible before changing versions.
actions: Resolve upstream source and commit
Restore exact Java, Gradle, loader, mappings, libraries, processors, and generated sources
For binary-only inputs, decompile twice and reconcile against bytecode
gates: A clean source build reproduces equivalent metadata and behavior

phases.title: Migrate mappings and namespaces
phases.goal: Translate names without hiding semantic API changes.
actions: Select one canonical mapping graph
Remap source or bytecode in an isolated branch
Diff APIs before replacing calls
gates: Mixin targets, refmaps, access wideners/transformers, and invokedynamic descriptors resolve

phases.title: Port loader and game APIs
phases.goal: Replace lifecycle, registry, networking, rendering, config, data, and side APIs deliberately.
actions: Port dependency declarations and entrypoints
Replace removed or behaviorally changed APIs
Separate common logic from loader adapters when appropriate
gates: Compile and static linkage pass on the native target loader
No compatibility bridge is the sole proof of correctness

phases.title: Transform data and assets
phases.goal: Preserve registries, tags, recipes, loot, models, shaders, translations, configs, and saved data.
actions: Diff pack/schema versions
Write explicit forward and reverse transforms
Measure downgrade loss on disposable copies
gates: World/data migration and rollback behavior are documented

phases.title: Compile and audit
phases.goal: Turn every build warning and static finding into an owned result.
actions: Run clean build with pinned Java
Run dependency convergence, duplicate-class, API diff, mixin, security, and SBOM checks
Reject undeclared or floating dependencies
gates: No unresolved critical/high finding is silently waived

phases.title: Exercise real client and server matrices
actions: Launch disposable client and dedicated server
Exercise networking, configs, registries, world creation/load, rendering, integrations, and highest-risk features
Inspect fresh logs and crash reports
gates: Feature-level acceptance checks pass with no new severe log evidence

phases.title: Package, compare, and retain rollback
phases.goal: Produce a reproducible artifact with complete lineage.
actions: Build twice from clean state
Compare archive contents and hashes
Write release, migration, loss, and restore receipts
gates: Rebuilds are byte-identical or differences are explained
Original and last-known-good artifacts remain restorable

verificationMatrix: Re-hash the selected input immediately before reconstruction and match SHA-256 bb7784ac47d400166dc3515e8f17b376c7baef4edb30b21b54b90ff78925606e.
Reconcile detected mod IDs, loader evidence, dependencies, mixins/access rules, nested JARs, signatures, and native libraries against the recovered source tree.
Compile from a clean dependency cache with the pinned Java and build toolchain.
Run static linkage, mixin/refmap, access widener/transformer, resource, and data schema checks.
Launch a disposable client and create/load a disposable world with fresh logs.
Launch a disposable dedicated server, join once, exercise networking/config sync, then stop cleanly.
Exercise the mod's highest-risk features, integrations, saved data, recipes, registries, and world generation.
Rebuild twice and compare package contents, hashes, embedded dependencies, signatures, and metadata.
completionDefinition: Source provenance is resolved independently, or binary-only reconstruction limitations are documented with dual-decompiler evidence.
No source, mapping, compile, linkage, mixin, resource, registry, data-fixer, network, or side-only failures remain.
Client and dedicated-server tests cover the mod's actual behavior rather than startup alone.
Upgrade and downgrade paths preserve documented data or explicitly report irreversible loss.
The original artifact and every mutation remain recoverable through hashes, receipts, backups, and rollback instructions.

workspace.rollback: Delete this isolated workspace; the installed mod was not changed.
